Summary

Voxtral 3 introduces a cutting-edge voice agent SDK and state-of-the-art speech models designed for real-time, multi-step conversations across 50+ languages. It combines accurate transcription, natural speech synthesis with emotional adaptability, and deep tool integration for seamless workflow automation. results.title: Mistral Voxtral 3 Posts 4.1% WER on FLEURS, Beating Whisper | AI Weekly
results.content:
The text-to-speech model, Voxtral Speech 3, is priced at $13 per million characters, covers 35+ languages and 50+ dialects, and clones a voice from 30+ minutes of audio with instruction following for emotion, pacing and emphasis. On price, Mistral writes that "Voxtral Speech 3 is positioned as more cost-effective than OpenAI TTS-1, Deepgram, ElevenLabs Flash, and Gemini Flash."

Deployment is through Mistral's EU-hosted API or self-hosting on private infrastructure, pitched as "sovereign deployment" with customer control over audio retention. The launch post publishes no per-language FLEURS breakouts and no customer names.

The release lands a day after Mistral's Timestral time-series model, making it the eleventh story we have tracked from the lab in the last three months. [...] Mistral says its new Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 hits 4.1% word error rate on the FLEURS 45 multilingual benchmark when the language is specified, and 4.0% when it is inferred, against 16.0% and 14.9% for Whisper large-v3. The claim sits in Mistral's launch post, which also names Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, Scribe v2 and GPT Transcribe as beaten on the same test. [...] The headline product is a voice agent SDK the company says "combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking into a real-time experience". Three transcription tiers sit under it: Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 at $0.0035 per minute, Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 at $0.004 per minute, and Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 at $0.008 per minute with sub-500ms latency. On the live-agent loop, the post states that "each turn completes in under one second, and the agent stops talking when the caller cuts in."

results.title: Mistral AI launches Voxtral 3, a full voice agent stack that listens, thinks, and talks in real time
results.content:
Oct 20, 2026

Mistral AI has launched Voxtral 3, a new family of language models built for real-time voice agents. The system includes a speech-to-text model (Voxtral Small Transcribe 3), a text-to-speech model (Voxtral Mini TTS 3), and a voice agent SDK based on LiveKit. Together, they combine listening, thinking, tool use, and speaking into a single streaming pipeline. Transcription covers more than 50 languages. Text-to-speech output supports over 35 languages and 50 dialects with emotional adaptation. Agents can tap into external systems during live conversations, for example, to book appointments or check invoices. [...] Mistral says the system can run on your own infrastructure or through EU-hosted APIs to keep data under your control. Pricing starts at $0.0035 per minute for transcription. More details are in the documentation.

results.content:
For developers and buyers, the near-term task is straightforward even if the long-term competitive picture is not: test Voxtral 3 against actual call recordings or use cases, confirm licensing and data residency terms directly with Mistral before any production commitment, and watch for the inevitable round of competitive price adjustments from OpenAI, Google, ElevenLabs, and Deepgram that a launch this direct is likely to provoke.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is Mistral Voxtral 3?  
Voxtral 3 is a family of four speech AI products from Mistral AI, covering batch and streaming speech-to-text, flagship transcription with added reasoning features, and text-to-speech, plus a voice agent SDK that connects all three into one real-time pipeline. [...] ## The Bigger Picture for AI Product Strategy

Voxtral 3 is a reminder that the AI product race is no longer only about which lab has the largest or smartest language model. Mistral is a company best known for open and efficient text models, and it chose to make its most aggressive, most specifically benchmarked competitive claims in voice, a category where it had no prior flagship product. That is a sign that speech and real-time agents have become a category worth fighting over on their own terms, separate from the general chatbot wars that dominated headlines through 2024 and 2025. [...] What makes Voxtral 3 worth tracking is not a single headline number. It is the combination of aggressive per-minute pricing, a LiveKit-based SDK built for live conversation rather than batch processing, and a set of claims that put Mistral directly up against OpenAI, Google, ElevenLabs, Deepgram, and Microsoft in the same breath. Mistral is betting that voice AI buyers care more about cost per minute and latency than brand name, and Voxtral 3 is the clearest test of that bet yet.
